tools.name: compare_engines
tools.description: Compare one page at one breakpoint in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. target (one view; the active view when absent) gives the breakpoint and the page; optional breakpoint (id), engines (chromium, firefox, webkit; all three when absent), url (http, https or file), threshold (colour tolerance 0 to 1), maxDiffPercent (0 to 100). Each engine shoots the viewport at the breakpoint's size and DPR - Chromium in a hidden render view, Firefox and WebKit in a window of their own - with its own user agent, and every engine pair is diffed; anti-aliased pixels (font smoothing) never count. An engine that cannot run (not installed, switched off) is listed under skipped, not an error. Answers when done: runId, folder (.rbrowser/out/engine-compare/<runId>/), report (report.html: side by side, slider, difference), each engine's shot path, and per pair status (same, differs, sizeMismatch, failed), percent, differentPixels, the diff image's path and the differing areas (x, y, width, height in pixels). One comparison at a time.

tools.name: script_run
tools.description: Run a short JavaScript that calls rBrowser's tools itself and answers only what it returns (MCP code mode): one call instead of a round trip per tool and view, the intermediate results never enter the context. code is the body of an async function with the parameters args (the JSON given as args) and target (as given, default "all"). Inside, await rb.<tool>(arguments) runs that MCP tool with exactly the guards of a direct call and gives its JSON answer; a refusal throws an Error named ToolError with code and tool. console.log lines come back as logs. Answer: result (the returned value as JSON), calls, durationMs, cut at mcp.scripts.maxResultBytes. The script runs in a sandbox: no fetch, require, import, timers, file system, network or process; at most mcp.scripts.maxCalls tool calls within mcp.scripts.timeoutMs. Off by default: a person switches it on with the setting mcp.scripts.enabled (code scripts_disabled). Failure codes: script.syntax (with line), script.timeout, script.call_limit, script.recursion (script_run inside a script), script.memory, script.stack, script.error or the tool's own code for an uncaught error (with name, tool, line). Example: await rb.navigate({ target, url: args.url }); const views = await rb.evaluate({ target, expression: 'document.documentElement.scrollWidth > innerWidth' }); return views.filter((v) => v.value).map((v) => v.breakpoint);

guard.note: Off until a person switches on the setting mcp.scripts.enabled (code scripts_disabled); every rb.* call inside runs through the same router and guards as a direct call, script_run itself is refused there (script.recursion), and a run is bounded by mcp.scripts.timeoutMs and mcp.scripts.maxCalls in a sandbox without file system, network or process.

Per view: vitals lcp, cls, inp, fcp and ttfb, each with value (ms; CLS unitless), rating ("good", "needs-improvement" or "poor" by web.dev's thresholds, overridable in vitals.thresholds) and the element behind it (lcp element, cls sources, inp target as CSS paths); resources cpuPercent (the page's main-thread share), memoryMb (its JS heap), cpuWarn and ramWarn (resources.cpuWarnPercent, resources.ramWarnMb); throttle (visible, hidden or cpuLimited); segment and soft (a soft navigation measures only CLS and INP). A missing value is {na, reason}: pending (not measured yet, e.g. INP before an interaction), unsupported or engine (the engine cannot give it; Firefox and WebKit views have no resources), soft, or off with the settingsKey that switched it off.

tools.name: view_page_zoom
tools.description: Zoom the page inside the targeted views as Chrome's Ctrl+Plus, Ctrl+Minus and Ctrl+0 do (Chromium's page zoom, not the grid's zoom of a cell). A zoomed page lays out at another CSS width than its breakpoint's, so breakpoints apply differently; the view's label strip shows the level. level: a factor (1 = 100 %, 0.25 to 5), "in" or "out" for one of Chromium's steps (25 % to 500 %); 100 % when absent. With the user setting views.pageZoom.sync every view takes the level; Chromium keeps a zoom per site, so views of one session on the same host zoom together. Chromium views zoom; a Firefox view zooms its Chromium stand-in in the grid only - Firefox's own window keeps the zoom its own keys and wheel give it; WebKit views do not zoom. target: "all", a view id or a breakpoint id; default the active view. Answers views: [{ view, level, percent }].

tools.name: views_force_state
tools.description: Force CSS pseudo-class states on a page element so it stays styled as hovered, focused or active while nothing touches it - e.g. keep a CSS hover menu (li:hover > ul) open in every view to measure or screenshot it. Chromium's CSS.forcePseudoState: hover, active and focus-within reach every ancestor too, as a real hover does; menus that open only through JavaScript (mouseenter) do not react. The element: a point (x, y in CSS px of the page's viewport, in `view`; rBrowser's own overlays are passed over) - the same element is found in the other targeted views by the sync's selectors - or a CSS selector, matched in each view. states: hover, active, focus, focus-visible, focus-within, visited, target; default ["hover"], [] takes the element's back. clear: true takes the element's states back, or without point and selector every forced state of the target (default then every view). States stay until cleared or the page navigates; the status bar says while states are forced. Only Chromium views. target: "all", a view id or a breakpoint id; default the active view. Answers views: [{ view, states } | { view, missing: true } | { view, error }] and forced: the views with forced states.
